findings.note: mustResultFile discards ParseResult's ignore-reason return value, so its stated contract ('a bad path exits 2 with nothing written', main.go:613-614) does not hold for an oversized result. ParseResult returns (zero value, reason, nil error) for a file over MaxResultBytes (256 KiB) at internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:151-153, and main.go:630 tests only err. Reproduced against a built binary in a scratch repo: metareview review pr-ready --base HEAD --shard-result <400 KB valid result JSON> exited 1, not 2, and wrote a run row plus a review log. Not blocking because shardpack Discover (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:332-336) re-parses the same bytes and the file surfaces in the review log under 'Ignored result files: result file exceeds 262144 bytes', so the operator is not left guessing; the coverage blocker still fires. Fix is to capture the reason and reject on it: if _, reason, err := ParseResult(data); err != nil || reason != "".

evidence.note: if _, _, err := reviewmanifest.ParseResult(data); err != nil — the middle (ignore reason) return value is dropped
oversized result returns a non-empty reason with a nil error, which is exactly the case mustResultFile cannot see
Discover turns the same non-empty reason into an IgnoredResult, which is why this stays advisory rather than silent

findings.note: handleOverride hand-rolls flag parsing instead of using the file's own flagValue helper, and silently tolerates a missing value. flagValue (main.go:467-473) exits 2 on both a missing value and a value that starts with '--'; the override loop (main.go:536-556) does neither, it just leaves the variable empty. The consequential case is a trailing --by: 'override request <id> --reason "..." --by' leaves by empty, main.go:559-561 then silently substitutes defaultActor() (the git user.email), and an audit record is written attributing the exception to an actor the caller did not name. Given that CLAUDE.md documents --by as the audit trail for who claims to have acted, a silent substitution on a truncated flag is the wrong default; exiting 2 the way every other flag in this file does would be correct. Adjacent cases (--reason with no value, a flag consuming the next flag as its value) currently fall through to the unknown-option branch or to override.go's own reason/actor validation, so they surface as errors, but with exit 1 rather than the exit 2 the rest of the CLI uses for usage errors.

evidence.note: case "--by": if i+1 < len(args) { by = args[i+1]; i++ } — a trailing --by is a no-op, no error
if by == "" { by = defaultActor() } silently attributes the override to the git identity
flagValue, the helper every other option in this file uses, exits 2 on a missing or flag-shaped value

findings.note: The fsmcli import is placed inside the standard-library group rather than the third-party group at cmd/metareview/main.go:8, between "fmt" and "os". gofmt -l is clean because the group happens to stay path-sorted, so nothing in CI catches it, but it breaks the grouping every other import block in the file and the repository follows and reads as an unreviewed auto-import. Cosmetic only, no behavioural effect.
